R0050.title: Risk Device Identification Bypass
R0050.definition: Modifying a real device's device information to deceive applications and lower the device risk score.
R0050.description: Scenarios include: the operating system running the app has been rooted, the app runs while being hooked, the app runs under a debugger, or the security certificate between the app and server has been replaced. Common risk device environments also include: injection via Hook frameworks such as Xposed/Frida, app cloning tools, device control systems, and tampering with device fingerprint information.
R0050.influence: May cause security processes within the application to be broken and data to be forged.

references.title: Cross-Border Fraud Risk: Analysis of Transnational Black-Grey Market Crime Patterns Driven by High Profits

observables: Device fingerprint reported fields exhibit injection traces from Hook frameworks such as Xposed and Frida
The same device fingerprint is reused or frequently switched across multiple different accounts within a short window
The device environment detects root, debugger attachment, or replaced security certificates
Device sensor data, system properties, or hardware identifiers exhibit spoofing characteristics of device-modification tools
Multiple accounts share the same underlying device characteristics under app-cloning or device-control environments

R0050-001.title: Virtual Device Identification Bypass
R0050-001.definition: Simulating a real device environment through software to bypass device identification and facilitate subsequent abuse.
R0050-001.description: Attackers run applications via cloud phones, cloud servers, virtual machines, emulators, anti-fingerprint browsers, and similar means, forging device fingerprints, sensor data, and hardware parameters so that risk-control systems recognize them as multiple independent real devices. This technique is often combined with device-control and device-modification tools to operate accounts in bulk, bypassing fingerprint-based risk control and one-device-one-account limits, and is widely used for bulk registration, account farming, and promo abuse.
R0050-001.influence: May cause security processes within the application to be broken and data to be forged.

observables: The device fingerprint matches known fingerprint databases for emulators, cloud phones, or virtual machines
Device hardware parameters such as CPU, GPU, and sensors exhibit synthetic characteristics of a virtual environment
The same virtual device instance hosts registration or login for a large number of different accounts within a short window
The IP, GPS, and device triples of anti-detect browsers or cloud phones exhibit batch-spoofed consistency
The device environment lacks real sensor fluctuation, with gyroscope and accelerometer data remaining static or constant over long periods
